dedupe_keys.name: faostat agri food systems emissions shares by country 1990 2019

description: This table gives, for every country, the greenhouse gas emissions of its food system and their share of total national emissions, broken down from the farm to household kitchens and food waste. The producer is the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, with Francesco Tubiello, Kevin Karl, Alessandro Flammini, Giulia Conchedda and colleagues, and the deposit is a snapshot of the FAOSTAT emissions shares database. Coverage is 236 countries and territories plus regional and world totals from 1990 to 2019, when food systems emitted about 16.5 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, 31 percent of the global total. Emissions are given by gas for farm-gate activities, land use change, and pre- and post-production stages including fertiliser manufacture, on-farm electricity, processing, transport, retail, packaging, household consumption and disposal of food waste. The long-format table is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: a 2022 snapshot, modelled estimates from national statistics, and FAOSTAT has since published newer releases. Simulation uses: quantifying energy and emission loads of food processing, cold chains and transport for climate scenario models of food supply. Related records: EDGAR-FOOD (data-edgar-food) is a comparable global inventory, and the European top-down model (data-eea-food-chain-emissions-top-down-model) gives country detail.
